batch_results.meta_observations: 1. Assessment instrument development and validation is the most dominant theme, appearing in nearly all abstracts. 2. There is a strong focus on psychometric properties and statistical rigor in the abstracts. 3. Competencies and skills (both technical and non-technical) are frequently assessed, reflecting a shift toward holistic engineering education. 4. Less emphasis is placed on resilience, online learning, and professional values, suggesting these are emerging or niche areas in this batch. 5. Many abstracts lack clear objectives, methods, results, or conclusions, limiting the depth of analysis.
batch_results.grounding_notes: 1. All themes are grounded in verbatim quotes from the abstracts. 2. Frequency is based on the number of abstracts explicitly mentioning the theme. 3. Confidence is 'high' for themes with clear and repeated evidence, 'medium' for themes with some evidence but less repetition, and 'uncertain' for themes with limited or indirect evidence. 4. No external frameworks or categories were imposed; themes emerged purely from the data.

themes.name: Assessment of Professional Competencies
themes.definition: The development, validation, and adaptation of instruments to measure professional competencies in engineering students, including technical, interpersonal, and ethical skills. Focuses on identifying and validating constructs such as employability, self-efficacy, and professional responsibility.
evidence: [LHGYXXJG] The study aims to identify indicators that can measure students' employability skills and attributes. The research model, based on The Conference Board of Canada (Employability Skills 2000+), is divided into fundamental skills, personal management skills, and cooperative skills.

[IV425BDL] Consequently, new competencies have been incorporated into engineering curricula, with ethics education emphasizing social responsibility as a core competency for students. This paper aims to adapt the 'Engineering Professional Responsibility Assessment (EPRA)' to Turkish culture.

[KI4LCCHP] This study aimed to validate the factor structure of professional competencies in engineering and test the measurement invariance of these competencies across gender. Through a cross-sectional survey, 552 senior undergraduate students responded to a 24-item professional competencies scale.

themes.name: Self-Efficacy Measurement in Engineering
themes.definition: The development and validation of scales to assess students' self-efficacy in engineering-related tasks, including programming, design, and general engineering skills. Focuses on the reliability and validity of these instruments across different contexts and demographics.
evidence: [2DDA52FC] Two scales for engineering self-efficacy have recently been developed for undergraduate students, with validity evidence relating self-efficacy responses to persistence and achievement in engineering.

[CJPX792Z] Contribution: This article has shown that self-efficacy in performing complex computer programming tasks and the self-regulation of electrical and electronics engineering undergraduate students varies with respect to the class standing and prior experience in computer programming.
[U374P6MT] The purpose of this study is to adapt a well-known self-efficacy scale and determine engineering student's C++ computer programming self-efficacy levels.

themes.name: Motivation and Learning Strategies Assessment
themes.definition: The validation and adaptation of instruments to measure students' motivational attitudes, learning strategies, and engagement in engineering education. Includes the use of Likert scales and factor analysis to assess constructs such as intrinsic and extrinsic motivation.
evidence: [CY59SPDS] This research paper reports the quantitative validation of instruments for assessing engineering students' motivational attitudes and behaviors in their capstone design course. Motivation plays a key role in engineering practice, particularly with respect to students' efficiency and effectiveness as well as their readiness to engage in teamwork.
[PYM3MQNK] The aims of this work were to investigate the dimensionality of the motivated strategies for learning questionnaire (MSLQ) and compare the validation of the three competing models.

[NLXE3X6S] Using the definition of sustainability from the Brundtland report and expectancy value theory, students’ sentiment toward SE was evaluated using items to assess SE self-efficacy, SE value and SE affect.

themes.name: Entrepreneurial Mindset and Design Skills
themes.definition: The development and validation of instruments to measure entrepreneurial mindset constructs, such as 'Connections' and 'Creating Value,' as well as design mindset and creativity in engineering students. Focuses on the use of factor analysis and confirmatory models.
evidence: [K9E5C83P] This Work in Progress paper will describe the initial steps of validating an instrument to measure Connections and Creating Value skills in undergraduate engineering students. Cultivating an entrepreneurial mindset and associated behaviors in first-year engineering students is one step towards fostering students' professional skill development.

[6XVSWITA] This article defines and operationalizes the construct design mindset and introduces the Design Mindset Inventory (D-Mindset0.1), allowing us to measure and leverage statistical analyses to advance our understanding of its role in design.

[YE4TP358] Creativity, being a key competency of engineering, must be taught and assessed. Here, we verify the reliability of the Creative Engineering Design Assessment (CEDA), a psychometric test for engineering students, as well as clarify the assessment process.

themes.name: Internship and Workplace Experience Evaluation
themes.definition: The adaptation and validation of instruments to assess students' perceptions of their internship and workplace experiences, including competencies developed and satisfaction with the learning environment. Focuses on the use of confirmatory factor analysis and reliability testing.
evidence: [DFVK7NR2] The purpose of this study was to validate a newly adapted version of the Work Experience Questionnaire (WEQ), which can be used for evaluating engineering students' perception of their internship experience.

[XHXW8PNL] The purpose of this paper is to assess engineering students’ perceptions of their internship experiences. For that purpose, the validation of a recently adapted version of the Work Experience Questionnaire (WEQ) was carried out on a sample of 447 engineering students.

[9CXV3IJ6] The apprenticeship course is suitable for trail and test under the supervision of academic educators and industry experts. The essential part of the practical skills training occurs during this period. In general, the apprenticeship course leads to acquiring valuable practical experiences and improving behavior and attitudes of students.

themes.name: Systems Thinking and Problem-Solving Skills
themes.definition: The assessment of systems thinking skills (STS) and problem-solving competencies in engineering students, including the use of surveys and diagnostic activities to measure these skills. Focuses on the development of instruments and cross-comparisons for validation.

[IQD3WXLQ] Industry-Coupled Problem-Based Learning (IC-PBL) has become a central approach in engineering education, enabling students to bridge theoretical understanding with real-world application.

themes.name: Communication Skills Assessment
themes.definition: The development and validation of instruments to measure workplace oral communication skills and other communication-related competencies in engineering students. Focuses on the use of factor analysis and reliability testing to ensure validity.

Among communication failures reported were oral communications, such as giving instruction and briefing; skills, which are supposed to be mastered by engineering graduates during their study years.

[XT6BBTKW] As there is currently no comprehensive measure that allows researchers, program evaluators, and outreach advisors to examine ambassadors' professional development and growth, this study sought to develop and validate an Ambassador Questionnaire (AQ).

themes.name: Mathematical and Technical Competence Measurement
themes.definition: The development and validation of instruments to assess mathematical and technical competencies in engineering students, including the use of Rasch analysis and think-aloud protocols to determine item difficulty and student ability.
evidence: [HX8CUXK4] This article reports about our efforts to determine engineering students' competence in mathematics. [VG98XEQP] In this research study, we are interested in assessing students' perceptions of working on a community-partnered project in their first year of engineering. The Likert scale questions included questions on engineering, design, and tinkering self-efficacy, intentions to persist, and sense of belonging scale.

batch_results.meta_observations: The abstracts predominantly focus on the development, validation, and adaptation of assessment instruments for engineering students. The most frequently observed themes include professional competencies, self-efficacy, and motivation. There is a notable emphasis on the use of factor analysis, confirmatory factor analysis, and reliability testing to validate these instruments. Some abstracts lack detailed methodological descriptions or results, which limits the depth of analysis for certain themes.
batch_results.grounding_notes: All themes and evidence are grounded in verbatim quotes from the abstracts. No external frameworks or categories were imposed. The frequency of themes is based on the number of abstracts explicitly addressing each theme. Some themes, such as 'Communication Skills Assessment' and 'Mathematical and Technical Competence Measurement,' are less frequently observed in this batch.

themes.name: Engineering Self-Efficacy Measurement
themes.definition: The development, validation, and comparison of instruments designed to assess engineering students' self-efficacy beliefs, including general vs. domain-specific constructs, and their reliability across contexts.
evidence: [LLIXIBSQ] This work investigates whether an engineering-domain specific self-efficacy measurement instrument is required for determining the self-efficacy beliefs of engineering students or whether a general instrument will suffice.

[B7B4X2WE] Self-efficacy has been linked to academic performance, motivation, and progression within engineering degree programs. Such associations are context specific, and an understanding of sources of self-efficacy is paramount to guiding policy and practice enhancements.

[QAJGLZ2K] This Research to Practice Full Paper outlines the process of converting the ABET Criterion 3 - Student Outcomes into an engineering self-efficacy scale (ESE-ABET) and in this format compares the current ABET 3.1-7 items with the previous ABET 3a-k items with undergraduate engineering students.

themes.name: Transferable and Vocational Competencies
themes.definition: The assessment and validation of non-technical skills (e.g., communication, teamwork, problem-solving) deemed essential for engineering graduates' employability and professional success.
evidence: [Y27Q6N9A] The focus of the assessment instrument was explicitly on 'above content' areas of the domain, and the assessment framework provides an example of a construct which articulates certain domain-specific competence components.

[DCSSFS2C] In an increasingly competitive labor market, transferable skills are becoming essential, particularly in engineering. Employers place growing importance on these skills, highlighting the need to assess current competency levels among engineering students.

[WWJJIDI6] Transferable skills are becoming increasingly important, due to a progressively more competitive labor market in an ever-changing world. Particularly in the engineering sphere, it is even more obvious, as technical skills need transferable skills to have value.

themes.name: Problem-Solving and Critical Thinking Assessment
themes.definition: The creation and validation of tools to measure engineering students' problem-solving abilities, critical thinking, and their development over time, including self-assessment instruments.
evidence: [BQS3WMHF] The EM-PSI is a student's self-assessment of their problem solving and critical thinking abilities broken down into three sub-categories, 1) problem solving confidence, 2) approach-avoidance style, and 3) personal control.

[XQ7RZDGG] This paper presents a new assessment tool for measuring an individual’s self-appraisal of their technical problem-solving ability and the initial validation of the tool using a pilot study involving 73 undergraduate Civil Engineering students and faculty.

[SFEN9MC6] The Transferable Learning Orientations (TLO) tool... is designed to engage students in meta-cognitive processes and provide meaningful feedback to students. The dimensions are outcome motivation, learning belief, self-efficacy, transfer and organisation.

themes.name: Contextual and Sustainable Competencies
themes.definition: The evaluation of competencies related to sustainability, ethics, and social responsibility within engineering education, including their integration into curricula and assessment tools.
evidence: [VSFBSRZB] The purpose of this work is to present a methodology for analyzing the perception of engineering students about the sustainability learning they have achieved during their university studies.

[LQ8RTKIQ] The integration of ethics, social responsibility, and sustainability (ERS) into higher education curricula is essential for fostering competencies aligned with the Sustainable Development Goals.

[C3YQG2PI] A challenge instructors face is developing and accurately assessing technical communication skills to ensure students can apply and transfer the skills from the academic context into the context of engineering practice.

themes.name: Instrument Development and Validation
themes.definition: The methodological process of designing, refining, and validating psychometric tools (e.g., scales, rubrics, questionnaires) to assess various competencies in engineering education.
evidence: [FL269LXE] This article provides comprehensive evidence of the content, structural, discriminant, and criterion-related validity of the contextual competence scale.

[FUDIEQYR] To meet the need for a very brief measure, a 5-item innovation self-efficacy (ISE.5) scale was developed using the 19-item Dyer et al. Innovative Behavior Scale (IBS) as a starting point, adapted for undergraduate engineering students, and then condensed using confirmatory factor analysis.

[QKJ5DVTR] This paper describes the development and validation of the Interprofessional Project Management Questionnaire (IPMQ) which has been designed for use in engineering education to provide a tool for reflection on, and clarification of, the learning goals related to these skills.

themes.name: Gender and Demographic Differences in Competencies
themes.definition: The examination of how gender, class level, transfer status, or other demographic factors influence self-efficacy, problem-solving abilities, or other measured competencies in engineering students.
evidence: [LLIXIBSQ] Furthermore, this study also aims to investigate the effect of gender, class level, and transfer status of students on their engineering self-efficacy beliefs.

[B7B4X2WE] Female students began the semester with significantly lower tinkering skills self-efficacy to male students, with female students general engineering self-efficacy increasing statistically more over the semester within a CDIO module.

[WHKSKTII] This work-in-progress research study examines the response patterns of first-generation college students (FGCS) to the engineering identity measures compared to non-first-generation college students (non-FGCS).

themes.name: Industry and Workplace Readiness
themes.definition: The assessment of competencies related to workplace readiness, including internships, employability skills, and alignment between academic training and industry expectations.
evidence: [5EXQUZSR] Industrial internships in vocational education are expected to support graduates' readiness to know the world of work according to their field of expertise.

[IUF35Z2I] Employability skills is a number of non-technical skills that are can be transferred into different fields of work, is required to enter the working world, to remain on the job, as well as developing a career in the workplace.

taxonomy.definition: The development, assessment, and validation of instruments to measure students' self-efficacy, identity, and sense of belonging in engineering contexts. This includes both general engineering self-efficacy and domain-specific self-efficacy (e.g., programming, design) as well as broader identity constructs like recognition and interest in engineering.
subthemes: General and domain-specific self-efficacy in engineering

taxonomy.theme: Ethical, Social Responsibility, and Professional Values
taxonomy.definition: The assessment of professional ethics, social responsibility, and dispositional values in engineering students. This includes evaluating understanding of ethical principles, sustainability, and global/societal impacts, as well as professional values aligned with engineering practice.
subthemes: Sustainability, ethics, and social responsibility competencies

taxonomy.theme: Motivational and Psychosocial Constructs in Engineering Education
taxonomy.definition: The measurement and validation of instruments assessing students' motivational attitudes, learning strategies, and psychosocial constructs (e.g., self-efficacy, attitudes) and their influence on educational outcomes. This includes both general motivational frameworks and specific constructs tied to engineering education.
subthemes: Psychosocial constructs and their influence on educational outcomes

taxonomy.theme: Workplace Readiness and Internship Competency Assessment
taxonomy.definition: The development and validation of instruments to assess students' competencies and experiences related to workplace readiness, internships, and alignment with industry expectations. This includes perceptions of internship experiences, employability skills, and readiness for professional practice.

The assessment of communication skills and other non-technical, transferable competencies essential for engineering graduates' employability. This includes workplace oral communication, teamwork, problem-solving, and critical thinking as broadly applicable skills.

The process of creating, refining, and validating tools (e.g., scales, rubrics, questionnaires) to measure specific competencies, attitudes, or skills in engineering education. This includes designing instruments, conducting pilot tests, and iteratively improving their structure and content based on empirical evidence.

The identification, assessment, and development of technical and non-technical (transversal) competencies required for engineering students. This encompasses professional skills, research competencies, and other transferable abilities essential for engineering practice.

The use of statistical methods to evaluate the validity, reliability, and structural properties of assessment instruments in engineering education. This includes techniques such as Cronbach's alpha, factor analysis, and structural equation modeling to ensure robust measurement.

The development and validation of instruments to measure entrepreneurial mindset constructs (e.g., 'Connections' and 'Creating Value') and design mindset in engineering students. This theme captures the intersection of innovation, creativity, and problem-solving in engineering education.

The assessment of systems thinking skills and problem-solving competencies in engineering students using surveys and diagnostic activities. This theme emphasizes the ability to analyze complex systems and develop effective solutions.

The development and validation of instruments to assess mathematical and technical competencies in engineering students, including the use of Rasch analysis and think-aloud protocols. This theme addresses foundational and advanced technical skills critical to engineering practice.

The examination of how gender, class level, transfer status, or other demographic factors influence self-efficacy, problem-solving abilities, or other measured competencies in engineering education. This theme explores disparities and variations in outcomes across different student groups.

taxonomy.theme: Leadership Competencies and Self-Efficacy in Engineering
taxonomy.definition: The development and validation of instruments to measure engineering students' leadership self-efficacy, including the identification of key leadership domains relevant to engineering contexts. This theme also examines the relationship between leadership confidence and broader professional competencies.

taxonomy.theme: Writing Attitudes and Affective Dimensions in Engineering Education
taxonomy.definition: The study of engineering students' attitudes, emotions, and apprehensions related to academic and professional writing, including the development of tools to assess and address writing challenges. This theme explores the impact of writing attitudes on career trajectories and educational outcomes.

The measurement of engineering students' confidence in performing specific tasks within biomedical engineering contexts, such as problem identification, engineering solutions, and grant proposal writing. This theme emphasizes the clinical and technical relevance of self-efficacy assessments.

notable_gaps: Limited coverage of demographic influences on engineering competencies (only 4 studies, 1 source batch)
Sparse evidence on leadership competencies and self-efficacy (1 study, 1 source batch)
Minimal research on writing attitudes and affective dimensions (1 study, 1 source batch)
Thin evidence on task-specific self-efficacy in specialized contexts like biomedical engineering (1 study, 1 source batch)
Low representation of mathematical and technical competence assessment (2 studies, 1 source batch)

_structural_signatures.name: Task-Specific Self-Efficacy in Biomedical Engineering
_structural_signatures.definition: The measurement of engineering students' confidence in performing specific tasks within biomedical engineering contexts, such as problem identification, engineering solutions, and grant proposal writing. This theme emphasizes the clinical and technical relevance of self-efficacy assessments.
